claim: Glutamine synthetase (GS) is the key enzyme of nitrogen assimilation induced under nitrogen limiting conditions.
source: Glutamine synthetase (GS) is the key enzyme of nitrogen assimilation induced under nitrogen limiting conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about GS function.

claim: The carbon skeleton of glutamate and glutamine, 2-oxoglutarate, is supplied from the TCA cycle.
source: The carbon skeleton of glutamate and glutamine, 2-oxoglutarate, is supplied from the TCA cycle, but how this metabolic flow is controlled in response to nitrogen availability remains unknown.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: The expression of the E1o component of 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase, SucA, is repressed under nitrogen limitation in Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli.
source: We show that the expression of the E1o component of 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase, SucA, is repressed under nitrogen limitation in Salmonella enterica and Escherichia coli.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 1B.

claim: The repression of SucA is exerted at the post-transcriptional level by an Hfq-dependent sRNA GlnZ generated from the 3′UTR of the GS-encoding glnA mRNA.
source: The repression is exerted at the post-transcriptional level by an Hfq-dependent sRNA GlnZ generated from the 3′UTR of the GS-encoding glnA mRNA.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Enterobacterial GlnZ variants contain a conserved seed sequence.
source: Enterobacterial GlnZ variants contain a conserved seed sequence and primarily regulate sucA through base-pairing far upstream of the translation initiation region.
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 2A and base-pairing analysis in Figure 3.

claim: GlnZ primarily regulates sucA through base-pairing far upstream of the translation initiation region.
source: Enterobacterial GlnZ variants contain a conserved seed sequence and primarily regulate sucA through base-pairing far upstream of the translation initiation region.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the base-pairing predictions and experimental validation shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: During growth on glutamine as the nitrogen source, the glnA 3′UTR deletion mutants expressed SucA at higher levels than the S. enterica and E. coli wild-type strains, respectively.
source: During growth on glutamine as the nitrogen source, the glnA 3′UTR deletion mutants expressed SucA at higher levels than the S. enterica and E. coli wild-type strains, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: In E. coli, the transcriptional regulator Nac also participates in the repression of sucA.
source: In E. coli, the transcriptional regulator Nac also participates in the repression of sucA.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the analysis of nac deletion mutants shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The release of GlnZ from the glnA mRNA by RNase E is essential for the post-transcriptional regulation of sucA.
source: Lastly, this study clarifies that the release of GlnZ from the glnA mRNA by RNase E is essential for the post-transcriptional regulation of sucA.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments with RNase E cleavage site mutants shown in Figure 6.

claim: Ammonia is the energetically most preferable nitrogen source.
source: Ammonia is the energetically most preferable nitrogen source and is assimilated via either glutamate dehydrogenase (GDH) or the glutamine synthetase (GS) and glutamine 2-oxoglutarate amidotransferase (GOGAT) pathway (Reitzer, 2003).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: GDH catalyzes the reductive amination of 2-oxoglutarate (2-OG, a.k.a. α-ketoglutarate) to glutamate (Glu) without ATP consumption.
source: GDH catalyzes the reductive amination of 2-oxoglutarate (2-OG, a.k.a. α-ketoglutarate) to glutamate (Glu) without ATP consumption.
evidence: This is stated as established biochemical knowledge.

claim: GS catalyzes the amidation of Glu to form glutamine (Gln) using one molecule of ATP.
source: In contrast, GS catalyzes the amidation of Glu to form glutamine (Gln) using one molecule of ATP, and then GOGAT transfers the amide group reductively to 2-OG to generate two Glu molecules, yielding one net Glu from 2-OG (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as established biochemical knowledge and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: GOGAT transfers the amide group reductively to 2-OG to generate two Glu molecules, yielding one net Glu from 2-OG.
source: In contrast, GS catalyzes the amidation of Glu to form glutamine (Gln) using one molecule of ATP, and then GOGAT transfers the amide group reductively to 2-OG to generate two Glu molecules, yielding one net Glu from 2-OG (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as established biochemical knowledge and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Nitrogen is limiting for most bacteria in freshwater, marine, and terrestrial ecosystems.
source: Nitrogen is limiting for most bacteria in freshwater, marine, and terrestrial ecosystems (Elser et al., 2007) and mammalian large intestines (Reese et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Nitrogen is limiting for most bacteria in mammalian large intestines.
source: Nitrogen is limiting for most bacteria in freshwater, marine, and terrestrial ecosystems (Elser et al., 2007) and mammalian large intestines (Reese et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The glnA gene is essential during invasion and proliferation in the host cells for S. enterica.
source: This regulation is particularly crucial for the facultative intracellular pathogen S. enterica since the GS-encoding glnA gene is essential during invasion and proliferation in the host cells (Popp et al., 2015; Klose and Mekalanos, 1997; Aurass et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The glnA gene constitutes an operon along with the glnLG genes encoding the NtrB/NtrC (GlnL/GlnG) two-component regulator system, which is conserved among enterobacteria.
source: The glnA gene constitutes an operon along with the glnLG genes encoding the NtrB/NtrC (GlnL/GlnG) two-component regulator system, which is conserved among enterobacteria (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The response regulator NtrC is phosphorylated by its cognate sensor kinase NtrB at a low nitrogen state.
source: The response regulator NtrC is phosphorylated by its cognate sensor kinase NtrB at a low nitrogen state and activates RpoN (σ54)-dependent promoters by binding at specific enhancer-like sequences (Ninfa and Magasanik, 1986; Ninfa et al., 1987).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: Phosphorylated NtrC activates RpoN (σ54)-dependent promoters by binding at specific enhancer-like sequences.
source: The response regulator NtrC is phosphorylated by its cognate sensor kinase NtrB at a low nitrogen state and activates RpoN (σ54)-dependent promoters by binding at specific enhancer-like sequences (Ninfa and Magasanik, 1986; Ninfa et al., 1987).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The glnALG operon contains three promoters, glnAp1, glnAp2, and glnLp.
source: The glnALG operon contains three promoters, glnAp1, glnAp2, and glnLp, and the proximal σ54-dependent promoter glnAp2 is activated by NtrC when phosphorylated by NtrB in nitrogen-poor conditions while the other σ70-dependent promoters are repressed by NtrC (Ueno-Nishio et al., 1984; Reitzer and Magasanik, 1985).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The proximal σ54-dependent promoter glnAp2 is activated by NtrC when phosphorylated by NtrB in nitrogen-poor conditions.
source: The glnALG operon contains three promoters, glnAp1, glnAp2, and glnLp, and the proximal σ54-dependent promoter glnAp2 is activated by NtrC when phosphorylated by NtrB in nitrogen-poor conditions while the other σ70-dependent promoters are repressed by NtrC (Ueno-Nishio et al., 1984; Reitzer and Magasanik, 1985).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The σ70-dependent promoters of glnALG operon are repressed by NtrC.
source: The glnALG operon contains three promoters, glnAp1, glnAp2, and glnLp, and the proximal σ54-dependent promoter glnAp2 is activated by NtrC when phosphorylated by NtrB in nitrogen-poor conditions while the other σ70-dependent promoters are repressed by NtrC (Ueno-Nishio et al., 1984; Reitzer and Magasanik, 1985).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The NtrB/NtrC system can be stimulated when the cells utilize Gln or low concentrations of ammonium as a sole nitrogen source in E. coli.
source: The NtrB/NtrC system can be stimulated when the cells utilize Gln or low concentrations of ammonium as a sole nitrogen source in E. coli (Schumacher et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: A low intracellular Gln level is perceived as nitrogen limitation to induce the transcription of glnA in S. enterica.
source: Still, it has been postulated that a low intracellular Gln level is perceived as nitrogen limitation to induce the transcription of glnA in S. enterica (Ikeda et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: 2-OG has been proposed as a plausible signaling compound coordinating carbon and nitrogen metabolism.
source: Alternatively, 2-OG has been proposed as a plausible signaling compound coordinating carbon and nitrogen metabolism since it serves as both the TCA cycle intermediary metabolite and the carbon skeleton of Glu and Gln (Huergo and Dixon, 2015).

claim: 2-OG serves as both the TCA cycle intermediary metabolite and the carbon skeleton of Glu and Gln.
source: Alternatively, 2-OG has been proposed as a plausible signaling compound coordinating carbon and nitrogen metabolism since it serves as both the TCA cycle intermediary metabolite and the carbon skeleton of Glu and Gln (Huergo and Dixon, 2015).

claim: 2-OG accumulates rapidly upon nitrogen limitation from 0.2 to 10 mM.
source: 2-OG accumulates rapidly upon nitrogen limitation from 0.2 to 10 mM (Yuan et al., 2009) and directly blocks glucose uptake by inhibiting enzyme I of the phosphoenolpyruvate phosphotransferase system (PTS) (Doucette et al., 2011).

claim: 2-OG directly blocks glucose uptake by inhibiting enzyme I of the phosphoenolpyruvate phosphotransferase system (PTS).
source: 2-OG accumulates rapidly upon nitrogen limitation from 0.2 to 10 mM (Yuan et al., 2009) and directly blocks glucose uptake by inhibiting enzyme I of the phosphoenolpyruvate phosphotransferase system (PTS) (Doucette et al., 2011).

claim: 2-OG inhibits cAMP synthesis by adenylate cyclase.
source: 2-OG also inhibits cAMP synthesis by adenylate cyclase (You et al., 2013).

claim: The genes under the direct transcriptional control of RpoN and NtrC have been extensively studied in S. enterica serovar Typhimurium and E. coli K-12.
source: The genes under the direct transcriptional control of RpoN and NtrC have been extensively studied in S. enterica serovar Typhimurium (Samuels et al., 2013; Bono et al., 2017) and E. coli K-12 (Brown et al., 2014; Zimmer et al., 2000), but none of the genes are implicated in the central carbon metabolism.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: None of the genes under the direct transcriptional control of RpoN and NtrC are implicated in the central carbon metabolism.
source: The genes under the direct transcriptional control of RpoN and NtrC have been extensively studied in S. enterica serovar Typhimurium (Samuels et al., 2013; Bono et al., 2017) and E. coli K-12 (Brown et al., 2014; Zimmer et al., 2000), but none of the genes are implicated in the central carbon metabolism.
evidence: This is stated with citation support.

claim: The regulons of alternative sigma factors and stress response regulators comprise coding and non-coding arms, the latter of which are mediated by small RNAs.

claim: The majority of sRNAs post-transcriptionally regulate target mRNAs through direct base-pairing in trans, which is facilitated by the RNA chaperone Hfq using multiple RNA-binding faces.
source: The majority of sRNAs post-transcriptionally regulate target mRNAs through direct base-pairing in trans, which is facilitated by the RNA chaperone Hfq using multiple RNA-binding faces (Vogel and Luisi, 2011; Updegrove et al., 2016; Kavita et al., 2018).

claim: 3′UTRs of mRNAs have emerged as a reservoir of post-transcriptional regulators.
